title: Sell Mineral Rights in Dora, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Dora, AL | Walker County
metaDescription: Own coal or coalbed methane minerals near Dora, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer for Walker County land in the Sipsey coal district.
heroLead: Dora sits in Walker County's Sipsey coal district, ground that's been mined, leased, and re-leased across more than a century of Alabama's coal and gas history.
intro: Underground mining operations and, later, coalbed methane development both touched land around Dora, and it's common for a current owner's mineral interest to trace back through more than one era of that history. We buy these interests directly and help sort out which layer of history applies to your specific tract.

Some Dora families hold a documented royalty history; others have only a deed reference to a reservation that's never generated a payment. We price both honestly rather than assuming one situation looks like the other.

sections.heading: Sipsey coalfield history near Dora
paragraphs: The Sipsey coal seams around Dora supported extensive underground mining for decades, and mineral acquisitions from that period frequently separated coal rights from both the surface and from any oil and gas rights, creating a title picture with more than one owner for the same tract.

sections.heading: Later coalbed methane leasing
paragraphs: When CBM operators arrived in the 1980s and 90s, they targeted the same coal seams for gas rather than solid extraction, sometimes requiring a separate lease from whoever held the gas rights specifically, distinct from the coal itself. We review deed language carefully to confirm which rights a current owner actually holds.

sections.heading: Tracing ownership through Walker County
paragraphs: Walker County's courthouse in Jasper holds the records needed to trace a Dora-area mineral interest through its various historical layers. We do that work before quoting, since an accurate picture of what you own matters more here than in areas with simpler title history.

faqs.question: Our deed mentions coal rights separately from oil and gas. Which one do we actually own?
faqs.answer: We review the specific deed language to determine what your family's interest actually covers, since coal and coalbed methane gas rights were sometimes held by different parties in this area.

faqs.question: Is there current CBM activity around Dora?
faqs.answer: Walker County has seen meaningful coalbed methane activity historically, and we check current well and permit records for the specific area around your tract before quoting.

faqs.question: How far back does the title chain usually go near Dora?
faqs.answer: Often a century or more, given the area's early coal mining history. We trace that chain through Walker County records to confirm current ownership.

faqs.question: Do you buy an interest even if we've never received a royalty payment?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many Dora-area interests we buy have no production history at all, and we price those against comparable lease and permit activity instead.
